summary.headline: Tata Elxsi Q4 FY26 revenue INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency; EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 130 bps QoQ; FY27 growth guided to higher single digit.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR993.8 crore, up 0.9% QoQ in constant currency, with transportation flat (+0.2% QoQ CC) and Media & Communications up 5.6% QoQ CC. Healthcare & Life Sciences fell 13.1% QoQ CC as expected deal awards slipped into Q1 FY27. EBITDA margin rose 130 bps QoQ to 24.6%, driven mainly by currency tailwinds (about 155 bps) partly offset by a salary increase (about 90 bps), with operating efficiencies adding about 65 bps. Management cut FY27 growth aspiration from double-digit to higher single-digit, with transportation expected to lead.

financial_highlights.change: Was below 70% at one point; nearly mid-70s

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Revenue flat (+0.2% QoQ CC) after recovery; OEMs now 77% of vertical revenue. Two strategic wins (new APAC new-age OEM, US next-gen mobility services company). Tier 1 portfolio shrinking; management sees growth coming from OEMs.

segments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Declined 13.1% QoQ CC as two large deals expected in Q4 slipped to Q1 FY27; a few projects closed. Opened an offshore development center for Terumo Corporation in the quarter.

segments.name: Media & Communication
segments.commentary: Grew 5.6% QoQ CC on deal ramp-ups, an AdTech deal and a Tier 1 US telco; won a multi-year large deal from a world-leading device OEM for video and broadband products, plus a large legacy-engineering takeover deal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth now expected in the higher single digits; double-digit aspiration withdrawn, with management saying it could change in the next 3-6 months.
Automotive: high-single-digit exit rate expected for FY27, not double-digit.
Margin: aim to exit Q4 FY27 at about 27% PBT margin (not full-year); current Q4 FY26 PBT margin cited as 25.6%. Margin improvement expected to be gradual QoQ.
Management expects FY27 to be a growth year with growth led uniformly across all three verticals.
capex_capacity: Utilization at about 73%; management sees capacity up to 80% to slightly above 80% before large hiring; headcount additions are being metered.
Hiring to be scaled in larger numbers once utilization reaches 80-82%.
Every 1% increase in utilization adds about 25-30 bps to margin, per CFO.

Incubating battery energy storage vertical (data centers, EV charging); aerospace & defence (HAL, ADA, global players) and manufacturing are early-stage investments, with one or two expected to show results in 4-6 quarters.
Opened offshore development center for Terumo Corporation in Q4.
demand_pricing: New customers contribute about 2-2.5% of revenue in any quarter; most revenue comes from existing customers. Ramp-ups take 9-12 months after a deal win.
Customers are increasingly seeking productivity-linked pricing; management says AI-driven productivity is both internal efficiency and a basis for better pricing power.
Some competitors priced contracts very aggressively; management is not seeing broad irrationality and says it is neither aggressive nor conservative on AI-linked bids.
GenAI conversations most active in media & telecom; in automotive and healthcare, focus is on cybersecurity and confidentiality, served by DevStudio.ai.
Tier 1 suppliers are shrinking as OEMs take more responsibility; some offshoring of projects during slowdowns is being seen.
Clients showing both deal wins and push-outs amid geopolitical uncertainty; no clear trend yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Healthcare fall and is Q4 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: Two large deals expected to close in Q4 slipped to Q1 after about six months of delay, though a few projects closed; management expects recovery in Q1 and says a few deals have already closed in the new quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 130 bps QoQ margin increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed about 155 bps to currency movements, about 65 bps to operating efficiencies and pyramid management, offset by about 90 bps from the January 1 salary increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company trading margin for growth on large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 27% reference is an exit PBT margin for Q4 FY27; large existing-customer deals may be priced competitively, but there is no company-wide guideline to drop margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management lowered its view to higher single-digit growth for FY27 from double-digit, with transportation expected to lead; this could change over 3-6 months depending on deal momentum.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift more business to fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed-price is a double-edged sword and it is not aiming for 70-80% fixed price; execution risk and revenue leakage are concerns.

qa_highlights.question: How much capacity is left before hiring?
qa_highlights.answer: At 73% utilization, capacity can go to 80% or slightly above; larger hiring is planned once utilization reaches 80-82%.

risks_watch: Healthcare recovery depends on closing the deals that slipped to Q1 FY27; the segment has declined for consecutive quarters.
Automotive growth expected to lag, with geopolitical uncertainty and Tier 1 shrinkage weighing on demand.
Pricing pressure from aggressive competitors, and possible AI-driven pricing pressure at contract renewals in 6-12 months.
Margin sustainability: part of the Q4 gain came from currency, and longer-tenure and fixed-price deals carry year-1 cost drag.
Media & Telecom remains volatile with consolidation-driven, cost-takeout deals; management says it is 'not out of the woods'.
Organic growth has been weak; ER&D projects run off at 10-15% of revenue per quarter and must be replaced by new wins.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term growth: management lowered FY27 guidance to higher single digit and described Healthcare as shifted rather than lost, while staying confident on margin direction and the long-term ramp of new deals. Answers on AI pricing and fixed-price risk were measured and balanced, with few hard numbers.
key_quotes: So I think I'm pretty hopeful that last quarter, Q4, was the bottom and we will be able to recover this.
I think maybe we would look at a high-single digit exit, may not get into a double-digit for automotive.
It is not our objective suddenly to move to a 70% or an 80% fixed price.
So every quarter, you will lose 10% to 15% revenues; you have to make it up with new contracts.

growth.why: FY27 growth cut from double-digit aspiration to higher single digit (~8% midpoint), with transportation leading and automotive exit high-single digit; backing is partial, relying on two strategic wins, ramp-ups of 9-12 months and utilisation rising from 73% toward 80%+ with hiring to follow, while Q4 revenue was only up 0.9% QoQ CC.
